spark.summary: SOLID, Clean Architecture, and KISS balance extensibility against simplicity: SOLID guides modular boundaries and dependency direction, Clean Architecture isolates domain rules from frameworks and databases, and KISS prevents premature abstraction.
spark.keyTakeaway: Apply Dependency Inversion at architectural boundaries (DB, HTTP, queues) while keeping internal domain logic direct and KISS-compliant.

concept.whyItMatters: Codebases rot in two opposite ways: 'Big Ball of Mud' monoliths where SQL queries and HTTP headers leak into business rules, or 'Enterprise FizzBuzz' over-engineering with 15 layers of interfaces for a CRUD endpoint. Knowing where to draw boundaries—and where to keep things dead simple—determines team velocity after year one.
whenToUse: Core domain services with complex business invariants (billing ledgers, order state machines, risk scoring) that must outlive framework or database migrations.
Multi-team backends where clear module interfaces (ISP/DIP) let teams deploy and test features independently.
Refactoring a 'God Service' where every PR triggers merge conflicts and breaks unrelated features.
whenNotToUse: Throwaway prototypes, hackathons, or one-off data migration scripts where KISS favors a single 150-line Python script.
Simple CRUD microservices with zero domain logic—forcing Clean Architecture's Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Presentation layers onto basic table wrappers adds 4x boilerplate.
Performance-critical tight loops (e.g., SIMD vector kernels, game physics) where virtual dispatch and object indirection hurt CPU cache locality.
keyPoints: SRP (Single Responsibility): A module should have one cohesive reason to change—tied to a single business actor or capability, not 'one method per class'.

OCP & LSP (Open/Closed & Liskov Substitution): Extend behavior via new implementations without breaking existing callers, and ensure subtypes honor the base contract's preconditions, postconditions, and exceptions.
ISP (Interface Segregation): Split fat interfaces (`UserService` with 20 methods) into focused role interfaces (`UserReader`, `CredentialVerifier`) so clients only depend on what they call.
DIP & Clean Architecture: High-level domain policies must not import low-level frameworks (SQLAlchemy, Spring Data, Kafka); both depend on domain-owned abstractions (Ports & Adapters).
KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid): Every abstraction carries cognitive and maintenance rent—only introduce interfaces, layers, or patterns when concrete complexity justifies them.

examples.title: Hexagonal / Clean Architecture Saved a Ledger Migration
examples.scenario: A fintech team needed to migrate its core settlement ledger from PostgreSQL to CockroachDB/DynamoDB without halting feature work.
examples.outcome: Because `SettlementEngine` only depended on a domain `LedgerPort` interface (DIP) and domain entities had zero JPA `@Entity` annotations, the team built and shadow-tested `DynamoLedgerAdapter` in 3 weeks with zero edits to settlement rules.

examples.title: Liskov Substitution Violation in File Storage
examples.scenario: A `ReadOnlyS3Store` subclass extended `BlobStore` and threw `UnsupportedOperationException` on `put(key, bytes)`.
examples.outcome: Background workers expecting `BlobStore` crashed at runtime. Splitting `BlobStore` into `ReadableBlobStore` and `WritableBlobStore` (ISP + LSP) caught invalid assignments at compile time.

tradeOffs.factor: Clean Architecture Layering vs. Development Speed
tradeOffs.pro: Domain logic stays 100% framework-independent, enabling millisecond unit tests and painless infrastructure swaps.
tradeOffs.con: Requires mapping DTOs across boundary layers (HTTP Request -> Command -> Domain -> DB Entity), adding boilerplate for simple endpoints.

tradeOffs.pro: Tiny, focused interfaces prevent mock bloat in tests and shield consumers from unrelated changes.
tradeOffs.con: Too many micro-interfaces fragment the codebase and make IDE navigation tedious.

tradeOffs.pro: Simple, concrete code is easy to read, debug, and delete when requirements pivot.
tradeOffs.con: Wait too long to extract seams in rapidly growing modules and you face painful 'shotgun surgery' refactors.

failureModes.name: Cargo-Cult Clean Architecture (4-Layer CRUD)
failureModes.description: Wrapping a 3-field `GET /health` or simple `UserProfile` CRUD in UseCase -> Interactor -> Port -> Mapper -> Adapter classes multiplies files by 5x with zero domain logic to protect.
failureModes.mitigation: Apply Clean Architecture selectively to rich domain modules; use Vertical Slice or simple Transaction Script for straightforward CRUD.

failureModes.name: LSP Contract Breakage
failureModes.description: A subclass overrides a method and strengthens preconditions, weakens postconditions, or throws unexpected checked/unchecked exceptions (e.g., `Square extends Rectangle`).
failureModes.mitigation: Favor composition over inheritance; run a shared contract test suite against all implementations of an interface.

failureModes.name: Anemic Domain Model
failureModes.description: Entities are reduced to pure getters/setters while all business rules sit in procedural `XxxManager` services, scattering invariants.
failureModes.mitigation: Co-locate state transitions and validation inside domain entities/aggregates (`order.cancel(reason)`) rather than external setter chains.

failureModes.name: Inverted Dependency Leakage
failureModes.description: Domain classes import Jackson `@JsonProperty`, JPA `@Entity`, or Protobuf generated types directly, coupling core rules to serialization and DB schemas.
failureModes.mitigation: Enforce package boundary rules in CI using ArchUnit (Java) or `import-linter` (Python) to fail builds if `domain` imports `infrastructure`.

commonMistakes: Interpreting SRP as 'every class can only have one public method', resulting in hundreds of fragmented 15-line classes.
Creating a 1:1 `FooService` + `FooServiceImpl` pair for every class in the repo when there is only one implementation (violating KISS).
Using inheritance just to share utility code instead of composition, leading to fragile base-class bugs.
Letting HTTP status codes or SQL `ResultSet` exceptions bubble straight into domain use-case signatures.
Ignoring KISS by designing generic rule engines for 3 static business rules.

sections.content:
## The idea

**SOLID** is a set of five object-oriented design heuristics coined by Robert C. Martin to keep modules cohesive and loosely coupled. **Clean Architecture** (and Hexagonal / Ports & Adapters) scales SOLID's Dependency Inversion Principle to the entire system: source-code dependencies must point *inward* toward pure domain rules, never *outward* toward databases, web frameworks, or third-party SDKs. **KISS** acts as the essential counterweight—reminding engineers that every abstraction has a cost and should only exist when it solves real, present complexity.

## Concrete walkthrough

Compare a tightly coupled checkout handler with a Clean Architecture + SOLID design:

1. **Before (Coupled)**: `POST /checkout` controller parses JSON, runs `SELECT * FROM inventory FOR UPDATE`, calls `StripeClient.charge()`, and sends an email—all in one 250-line method. Testing requires Postgres + Stripe WireMock.
2. **After (Clean + SOLID)**:
   - **Domain Layer**: `Order` aggregate enforces invariants (`order.confirmPayment(receipt)`). Zero imports from Spring, Jackson, or JDBC.
   - **Application Layer**: `CheckoutUseCase` orchestrates the flow using two **Ports** (interfaces): `InventoryPort` (ISP-sized: `reserve(sku, qty)`) and `PaymentPort` (`charge(money, token)`).
   - **Infrastructure Layer**: `PostgresInventoryAdapter` and `StripePaymentAdapter` implement those ports (DIP), translating domain objects to SQL and Stripe SDK calls.
   - **KISS Check**: Simple read-only endpoints like `GET /orders/{id}` bypass the heavy use-case ceremony and query a lightweight read projection directly (CQRS-lite).

sections.content:
## Enforcing boundaries automatically

Architectural guidelines decay under deadline pressure unless enforced in CI. In Java, **ArchUnit** lets you write a 10-line JUnit test asserting `noClasses().that().resideInAPackage("..domain..").should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAnyPackage("..infrastructure..", "org.springframework..")`. In Python, **import-linter** enforces similar `forbidden` or `layers` contracts in `pyproject.toml`. Automated fitness functions turn Clean Architecture from a slide-deck aspiration into a build-time guarantee.

## SOLID principles at a glance

| Principle | Core Rule | Concrete Violation | Practical Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SRP** (Single Responsibility) | One cohesive actor/reason to change | `UserService` handles auth, PDF invoices, & emails | Split into `AuthService`, `InvoiceGenerator`, `EmailNotifier` |
| **OCP** (Open/Closed) | Extend via new code, not editing core switches | Adding a new tax rule edits 6 `if/else` blocks | Extract `TaxRule` interface & register implementations |
| **LSP** (Liskov Substitution) | Subtypes must honor base behavior contracts | `ReadOnlyRepo.save()` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` | Split `ReadRepository` & `WriteRepository` |
| **ISP** (Interface Segregation) | Clients shouldn't depend on unused methods | 18-method `CloudStorage` interface | Split into `BlobReader`, `BlobWriter`, `BucketAdmin` |
| **DIP** (Dependency Inversion) | High-level policy depends on abstractions | `BillingEngine` imports `psycopg2` directly | Define `LedgerPort` in domain; implement in infra |

## Failure modes

- **Abstraction Astronautics (Violating KISS)**: Creating `GenericRepository<T, ID>` + `AbstractBaseService<T>` for every table adds layers that fight SQL joins, batch updates, and query tuning.
- **Leaky Abstractions**: Returning Spring Data `Page<T>` or SQLAlchemy `Query` objects from a domain port leaks framework types into the core.
- **Transaction Boundary Confusion**: Placing `@Transactional` on small repository methods instead of the Application UseCase causes partial commits when step 2 of 3 fails.
- **LSP Exceptions in Mocks/Stubs**: Test doubles that behave differently from production adapters (e.g., ignoring unique-constraint checks) give false green builds.

## Balancing Clean Architecture with KISS

Not every module needs full Hexagonal ceremony. Use **Vertical Slice Architecture** or **Pragmatic Layering**: reserve pure Domain + Ports & Adapters for the 20% of your system that holds complex business rules, money movement, or volatile external integrations. For admin dashboards, reporting queries, and simple CRUD, let a lightweight handler query the database directly via a clean SQL/jOOQ/SQLAlchemy layer. Simplicity is a feature.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Keep domain entities and value objects free of ORM, HTTP, and serialization annotations.
- [ ] Only introduce an interface when you have >=2 implementations, an I/O boundary to fake in tests, or an explicit plugin seam.
- [ ] Enforce package dependency direction in CI using ArchUnit or `import-linter`.
- [ ] Place transaction boundaries (`@Transactional` / `async with session.begin()`) at the Application UseCase layer, not inside individual repositories.
- [ ] Review PRs with a KISS filter: ask 'what concrete problem does this new layer solve today?'

interviewProblems.title: Architectural Defense: Scaling SOLID Principles, Clean Architecture & KISS
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: You are leading the design of a distributed application encountering bottlenecks in Software Design & Architecture. How do you leverage SOLID Principles, Clean Architecture & KISS to guarantee high availability?

dimensions.name: Pattern Selection & Execution
dimensions.description: Applying SOLID Principles, Clean Architecture & KISS effectively.

interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Deploy SOLID Principles, Clean Architecture & KISS with strict monitoring thresholds and graceful degradation fallbacks.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: SOLID, Clean Architecture, and KISS balance extensibility against simplicity: SOLID guides modular boundaries and dependency direction, Clean Architecture isolates domain rules from frameworks and databases, and KISS prevents premature abstraction.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Order Domain Model applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Postgres & Stripe Adapters.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Postgres & Stripe Adapters experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Apply Clean Architecture selectively to rich domain modules; use Vertical Slice or simple Transaction Script for straightforward CRUD.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Apply Dependency Inversion at architectural boundaries (DB, HTTP, queues) while keeping internal domain logic direct and KISS-compliant.
Avoid trap: Interpreting SRP as 'every class can only have one public method', resulting in hundreds of fragmented 15-line classes.
Avoid trap: Creating a 1:1 `FooService` + `FooServiceImpl` pair for every class in the repo when there is only one implementation (violating KISS).
When to reach for it: Core domain services with complex business invariants (billing ledgers, order state machines, risk scoring) that must outlive framework or database migrations.
When to reach for it: Multi-team backends where clear module interfaces (ISP/DIP) let teams deploy and test features independently.

putItTogether.title: Putting Design Principles Solid Together
putItTogether.summary: Apply Dependency Inversion at architectural boundaries (DB, HTTP, queues) while keeping internal domain logic direct and KISS-compliant.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Design Principles Solid before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Because `SettlementEngine` only depended on a domain `LedgerPort` interface (DIP) and domain entities had zero JPA `@Entity` annotations, the team built and shadow-tested `DynamoLedgerAdapter` in 3 weeks with zero edits to settlement rules.
